reader.requirement: At 1985 data-name-2 and data-name-3 may be written qualified (format 1 of §1985:IV.4.3.8.1: group, record and file-name qualifiers, in successively more inclusive order, any sufficient subset), and a name that is not unique must be qualified to be referenced.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel >= 2002: record subtree with implicit superordinate qualifiers; below 2002 the whole scope's candidates, so an unqualified name also declared in another record is ambiguous (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 1985 an unqualified operand whose name is also declared in another record is refused as ambiguous (COBOL1639) and needs a qualifier; from 2002 the record's own subtree is the candidate set (§2002 F.2 item 67)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: group and record qualifiers in WS; not exercised are the file-name qualifier, a qualifier over an FD record, a name ambiguous across records, and wrong or misordered qualifiers

probes.expected: qualifiers by record (OF W), by group, record and file-name (FB OF FS1 OF FREC OF F1 THRU FA IN FS2 IN F1) and FS2 OF F1 accepted, ranges as GR1/GR2

probes.printed: error COBOL1639: 'WR1' RENAMES 'X' does not uniquely identify a data item — 2 declarations match (ISO §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR3 ...)
probes.expected: X is declared in V and W: uniqueness must be established through qualification

probes.printed: error COBOL1655: 'WR1' RENAMES X THRU Y: 'X' does not name an item of the record
probes.expected: X OF G2: G2 is no superordinate of X, refused

probes.printed: error COBOL1655: 'WR1' RENAMES X THRU Y: 'X' does not name an item of the record
probes.expected: X OF W OF G1: qualifiers not in successively more inclusive order (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1 rule 4), refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR5  (║5.11.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR5
OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1  (4.3.8.1 Qualification)  the text is in the clause; it lies in SR3

reader.notes: The operand capture keeps the IN/OF chain and the one qualifier walk matches group, record and file-name qualifiers; the 1985 arm (whole-scope candidates) is the one the 1985 uniqueness rule asks for. The unresolved-qualifier diagnostic says 'does not name an item of the record' rather than naming the qualifier, a wording matter, not a verdict one.

refuter.evidence: Probed qualifier kinds the reader did not: an SD file-name qualifier (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/rn_sd.cob: '66 SR2-Q RENAMES SV2 OF SR2 OF SF' binds, Q=AAA/BBB from the sorted records), a cd-name and record qualifier (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/rn_cd.cob: 'CS1 OF CREC OF CIN THRU CS2 IN CIN' binds), a linkage record (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/rn_link.cob), and a qualifier pair that picks two same-word items of one record (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/rn_sameword.cob: 'X OF G1 THRU X OF G2' and 'Y THRU X IN G2' bind to the right items: R1=AABBCC R2=BBCC). The reader's probes cover the ambiguous unqualified name (COBOL1639), a qualifier that is no superordinate and a misordered chain (COBOL1655). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR5 ... the text is in SR5'. Qualification itself works for every 1985 record kind; the doubt about the same word is SR4's (see that case), not SR5's.
